parsed.population_and_sample: 97 survey respondents (mixed, age 18+), and a sample of 24 male and 32 female users in the time-measurement component.
parsed.exposure: Public toilet provision models (quantitative regulation vs. potty parity) and institutional governance practices.
parsed.outcome: Toilet access, specifically waiting times, perceived safety, and care-related accessibility constraints.
parsed.rationale: The study provides empirical evidence (survey and time-measurement) on how legal and regulatory standards for public toilet provision impact access inequality, specifically addressing gendered time costs and institutional accountability.
